sources.entry: AdGuard Home - User-friendly ads & trackers blocking DNS server. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker
AdGuard Home | Network-wide ad and tracker blocking DNS server

summary.one_liner: AdGuard Home is a free, open-source, network-wide ad and tracker blocking DNS server that covers every device on a home network without client-side software.
summary.what_it_does: It runs as a DNS server that re-routes tracking and ad domains to a "black hole", so devices on the network cannot connect to those servers. Setup is done once on the network rather than on each device. The README describes a web admin interface, configurable blocklists, custom filtering rules, per-client configuration, and a built-in DHCP server. It supports encrypted upstream DNS (DNS-over-HTTPS, DNS-over-TLS, DNSCrypt) and can run as a DNS-over-HTTPS or DNS-over-TLS server. It also lists blocking of phishing/malware domains, adult-domain parental control, forced safe search, and running without root privileges. The project offers a REST API and a Python client for integrations, and it collects no usage statistics by default.
use_cases: block ads on every device in my home network
block trackers on smart TVs and IoT devices
run my own private DNS server
parental control by blocking adult domains
encrypted DNS upstream for home network
how_to_run: docker pull the official AdGuard Home image from Docker Hub (URL not included in README text)
snap install from the Snap Store (Linux)
git clone the repository, cd AdGuardHome, then run make (requires Go 1.25+, Node.js 24.10.0+, npm 10.8+)
notable: Network-wide blocking with no client software needed on each device, including IoT and smart TVs
Built-in encrypted upstream DNS (DoH, DoT, DNSCrypt) and option to act as a DoH/DoT server, per the README comparison table
Built-in DHCP server and per-client configuration in one package
Shares code with the public AdGuard DNS servers, per the README
README includes a feature comparison table against Pi-hole
caveats: DNS-level blocking cannot remove ads that share a domain with content, such as YouTube or Twitch ads and sponsored social media posts (README 'Known limitations')
Building from source requires Go 1.25+ and Node.js 24.10+; the README warns that make -j is not supported
Installation options listed cover Linux, Unix, macOS, FreeBSD and OpenBSD via script; other platforms are described as needing manual installation via the Wiki
